chapter_title_en: The Line That Cannot Be Crossed
chapter_seo_title: Ancestor Xuanji Demands Ji Ning – Black-White College Refuses – The Line Is Drawn
chapter_meta_description: Ancestor Xuanji storms the Black-White College, demanding they hand over Ji Ning. But eight elite Loose Immortals hold firm, and a long-lost Celestial Immortal draws the political line.
og_title: Black-White College Refuses to Hand Over Ji Ning – No Matter the Cost
og_description: The battle for Ji Ning becomes a political war. Xuanji threatens the sect. Tuoshan appears. The line is drawn in Anchan Commandery.
twitter_title: The Sect That Refused to Hand Over Its Disciple
twitter_description: A Celestial Immortal from the dead appears to draw the line. The Black-White College stands firm. Ji Ning is reading in the rain.

lore_anchors.definition: The highest tier of immortal in the Xianxia cultivation system, who has transcended life and death after passing the Heavenly Tribulation. In Desolate Era, they are ancient powerhouses commanding immense cosmic authority and feared even by imperial dynasties.

A cultivator whose physical body was destroyed during the Heavenly Tribulation, surviving only in spirit form. They are weaker than Celestial Immortals and must face escalating tribulations every few hundred thousand years.

A high-level Dao comprehension state where a cultivator projects their understanding of the Grand Dao of the Sword as a persistent field of influence, granting overwhelming offensive power in their vicinity.

A high-order metaphysical law governing a fundamental aspect of reality—one tier below the Supreme Heavenly Dao. Mastering a complete Grand Dao is a prerequisite for breaking through to the Primal or Earth Immortal level in elite sects.
A phenomenon where a cultivator's soul aligns with a specific truth of the Dao, causing the physical environment to react—rain, light, wind—as a sign of deep, qualitative breakthrough.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the Black-White College refuse to hand over Ji Ning?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In Xianxia culture, a sect that abandons its own disciples loses all face and credibility. The college's reputation would be shattered, and no future genius would ever join them.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Tuoshan able to stop Xuanji?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Tuoshan is a Celestial Immortal from the Northmont Clan, the ruling feudal lords of Anchan Commandery. Even the stronger Shaoyan Clan cannot start a war inside a vassal's territory without triggering an imperial response from the Grand Xia Dynasty.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn't the Black-White College help Ji Ning directly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Tuoshan warns them not to, because a full-scale war between the Shaoyan Clan and the Black-White College would destroy the sect. They can protect him inside the college, but outside, Ji Ning is on his own.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is Ji Ning doing while all this politics happens?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is inside the Aquatic Manor, reading the Starseizing Scrolls. The Yellow-haired Bear forces him to calm his Dao-heart before discussing anything, leading to a spontaneous Dao-resonance rainfall.
